citation: Landry, S. H., Zucker, T. A., Montroy, J. J., Hsu, H.-Y., Assel, M. A., Varghese, C., Crawford, A., & Feil, E. G. (2021). Replication of combined school readiness interventions for teachers and parents of head start pre-kindergarteners using remote delivery. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 56, 149-166. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2021.03.007
report_number: Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 56, 149-166 (peer-reviewed journal article; no IES/EEF report number). IES-funded under U.S. Department of Education grant R305A140386.
design: Cluster-RCT; assignment at the teacher/classroom level (Head Start pre-k); four-group 2x2 factorial (eTEEM x ePALS) replicating Landry et al. 2017 in REMOTE-delivery form: online classroom PD (eTEEM = online The Early Education Model) crossed with an online parent/home program (ePALS = online Play and Learning Strategies). 40 Head Start schools, 1 classroom each (n=69 initial; 76 unique teachers after replacements; 68 classrooms at posttest = 36 eTEEM/32 No eTEEM). Children at-risk 3-5 yr in Head Start; analytic child sample n=630 (452 completed posttest). Subjects: early literacy, language, math (plus self-regulation & social-behavioral, not extracted). Pre-K, Low SES.
problems: FACTORIAL DESIGN -> the requested TPD-vs-no-TPD (classroom-PD) contrast is the MAIN EFFECT OF eTEEM, reported directly in Table 4 (p. 160) as an adjusted least-square-mean difference (b) and a Hedges' g. Because the design is a 2x2 (eTEEM x ePALS) crossed factorial, the eTEEM main effect collapses across the ePALS factor, i.e. it compares the two eTEEM cells (eTEEM/No ePALS + eTEEM/ePALS) against the two No-eTEEM cells (No eTEEM/No ePALS [pure control] + No eTEEM/ePALS). This is the appropriate marginal contrast for 'classroom TPD vs no classroom TPD'; there is no single pure business-as-usual two-arm comparison, and the eTEEM x ePALS interaction was non-significant for every academic outcome (interaction g range -0.23 to 0.30, only EOWPVT at trend p=0.09), so the marginal eTEEM main effect is a clean estimate of the classroom-PD effect. All six academic outcomes were extracted (5 of them with skip applied only to teacher/parent/self-reg/social-behavioral outcomes per spec). Models are ANCOVA mixed models (maximum-likelihood, parent/child nested in classroom) controlling for pretest, child gender, age, and home language -> pretest_adjusted=true and cluster_adjusted=true. The authors computed Hedges' g themselves (Table 4 footnote b: 'computed using posttest raw score means and pooled standard deviations'); these g values are reproduced. NO standard error / variance for the impact estimate or for g is reported in Table 4 and posttest SDs by eTEEM/No-eTEEM are in online Supplementary Table A13 (not in the downloaded PDF), so g_var/g_se are null and cannot be computed from the available pages. NO design-effect ICC for child academic outcomes is reported (the ICCs of 0.80/0.62 in the text are inter-rater reliability for teacher observation tools, NOT clustering ICCs) -> icc=null (never guessed). n_t/n_c are the analytic-sample cell sums (eTEEM=151+186=337; No eTEEM=133+160=293; total n=630); posttest-completer cell sums were eTEEM=112+121=233 and No eTEEM=102+117=219 (see per-effect notes). n_clusters=68 (36 eTEEM / 32 No eTEEM at posttest). Distinct from Landry et al. 2014 and Landry et al. 2017 (this is the 2021 remote-delivery conceptual replication of the 2017 in-person study). TEMA math main effect of eTEEM was at trend (g=0.18, p<0.06); all other academic eTEEM main effects were non-significant.
